Εὐθέως δὲ παρεκέλευσε τοὺς ἐπισκόπους τὴν ζήτησιν
τοῦ ποθουμένου ξύλου ποιήσασθαι. Ἀπορούντων δὲ πάντων ἐπὶ τοῦ τόπου, καὶ
ἄλλου ἄλλο ὑποψίας διηγουμένου, ὁ τῆς πόλεως ἐπίσκοπος πάντας παρεκάλει
ἡσυχίαν ἄγειν, καὶ σπου δαιοτέραν εὐχὴν ὑπὲρ τούτου τῷ Θεῷ προσφέρειν.Τούτου
δὲ γενομένου, εὐθέως ἐδείχθη θεόθεν ὁ τόπος τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ, ἐν ᾧ ἵδρυτο τοῦ
ἀκαθάρτου δαίμονος ὁ ναὸς καὶ τὸ ἄγαλμα.
Τότε ἡ βασίλισσα, τῇ βασιλικῇ αὐθεντίᾳ χρωμένη, συναγαγοῦσα πλῆθος πολὺ
τεχνιτῶν καὶ ἐργατῶν, ἐκέλευσεν ἐκ βάθρων ἀνατραπῆναι τὸ μυσαρὸν οἰκο δόμημα,
καὶ τὸν χοῦν πόῤῥω που ἀποῤῥιφῆναι. Τούτου δὲ γενομένου, ἀνεφάνη τὸ θεῖον
μνῆμα, καὶ ὁ τόπος τοῦ Κρανίου, καὶ οὐ μήκοθεν τρεῖς σταυροὶ κεχωρισμένοι·
ἐπιμελῶς δὲ ἐρευνήσαντες εὗρον καὶ τοὺς ἥλους.Ἐκεῖθεν λοιπὸν ἀμηχανία καὶ
θλίψις κατέλαβε τὴν βασίλισσαν, ἐπιζητοῦσαν, ποῖος ἄρα εἴη ὁ ∆εσποτικὸς σταυρός.
Ὁ δὲ ἐπίσκοπος διὰ πίστεως τὴν διάκρισιν ἔλυσεν. Γυναικὶ γὰρ ἀῤῥωστούσῃ τῶν
ἐμφανῶν, καὶ ἀπεγνωσμένῃ ὑπὸ πάντων, καὶ τὰ τελευταῖα πνεούσῃ, προσαγαγὼν
ἑκάτερον τῶν σταυρῶν, τὸν ζητούμενον ηὗρεν· μόνον γὰρ ἤγγισεν ἡ σκιὰ τοῦ
σωτηρίου σταυ ροῦ τῇ ἀσθενούσῃ, εὐθὺς ἡ ἄπνους καὶ ἀκίνητος θείᾳ δυνάμει
παραχρῆμα ἀνεπήδησεν καὶ μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ βοῶσα, καὶ δοξάζουσα τὸν Θεόν.Ἡ δὲ
βασίλισσα Ἑλένη τῇ φωνῇ βοῶσα καὶ δοξά ζουσα τὸν Θεὸν, μετὰ χαρᾶς μεγάλης καὶ
φόβου ἀν ελομένη τὸν ζωοποιὸν σταυρὸν, μέρος μέν τι σὺν τοῖς ἥλοις ἀνεκόμισε
πρὸς τὸν παῖδα. Τῷ δὲ λοιπῷ γλωσ \σόκομον ἀργυροῦν ποιήσασα, παρέδωκε τῷ
ἐπισκόπῳ τῆς πόλεως, εἰς μνημόσυνον πάσαις γενεαῖς, καὶ θεσπίσασα ἐκκλησίαν
γενέσθαι ἐν τῷ ζωοποιῷ μνή ματι καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ Γολγοθᾷ καὶ ἐν τῇ Βηθλεὲμ ἐν τῷ
σπηλαίῳ, ἔνθα ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τὴν κατὰ σάρκα γέννησιν ὑπέμεινε,
καὶ ἐν ὄρει τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, ἔνθα ὁ Κύριος εὐλογήσας τοὺς μαθητὰς ἀν ελήφθη. Καὶ
ἄλλα πολλὰ ποιήσασα ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις, ἀνέστρεψε πρὸς τὸν παῖδα.Ὁ δὲ μετὰ χαρᾶς
αὐτὴν ὑποδεξάμενος, τὴν μὲν 4081 τοῦ τιμίου σταυροῦ μερίδα ἐν χρυσῇ θήκῃ
ἀποθέμε νος, παρέδωκε τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ εἰς τήρησιν, ἐνιαυσίαις μνήμαις ἑορτάζειν τὴν
ἀνάδειξιν τοῦ τιμίου σταυροῦ προστάξας. Τῶν δὲ ἤλων τοὺς μὲν εἰς τὴν ἰδίαν περι
κεφαλαίαν ἐχάλκευσεν, τοὺς δὲ ἀνέμιξε τῷ συμβα ρίῳ τοῦ ἵππου αὐτοῦ, ἴνα
πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν τοῦ Κυρίου διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· «Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ,
ἔσται τὸ ἐπὶ τὸν χαλινὸν τοῦ ἵππου, ἅγιον Κυρίῳ παντοκράτορι.»Ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς
ἔγραψε ἐπισκόπῳ Μακαρίῳ ἐπισπεύδειν τὴν οἰκοδομὴν, καὶ ἄρχοντα τοῦ ἔργου
ἀπέστειλε μετὰ δαψιλείας χρημάτων, παραγγείλας αὐτῷ φιλοτίμως κτισθῆναι τοὺς
ἁγίους τόπους, ὡς μὴ εἶναι τοιαύτην καλλονὴν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ. Ἔγραψε δὲ καὶ τοῖς
ἡγεμόσι τῆς ἐπαρχίας παντοίως συνελθεῖν τῷ ἔργῳ ἐκ τοῦ δημοσίου λόγου, ἔν τε
χρήμασι καὶ ἀναλώμασι καὶ ὕλαις. Ἦν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς φαιδρῶς ἄγων τῆς
εἰκοσαετηρίδος τὴν ἑορτὴν, εὐχαριστῶν τῷ Θεῷ ὑπὲρ πάντων τῶν ἀγαθῶν, ὧν
ἐποίησεν ἐν τοῖς χρόνοις τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ. Συνάγονται δὲ τὰ ἔτη ἀπὸ μὲν
Χριστοῦ παρουσίας ἕως τῆς εὑρέσεως τοῦ σταυροῦ, τριακόσια πεντήκοντα δύο ἔτη.
Ἀπὸ δὲ Ἀδὰμ ἕως παρουσίας Χριστοῦ, ἔτη πεντακισχίλια πεντακόσια. Καθ' ἑτέρους

Μακάριον διεδέξατο Μαξιμωνᾶς. Οὗτος δὲ πρᾶος ἀνὴρ καὶ ἐπίσημος λίαν. Ἐν γὰρ τῷ
διωγμῷ πολλὰς βασάνους ὑπέμεινε διὰ τὸν Θεὸν, καὶ τὸν δεξιὸν ὀφθαλμὸν

thought_title: Helena finds the Cross and Constantine spreads its veneration
orientation: The narrator is recounting how, after Helena arrived in Jerusalem and was received by Bishop Macarius, the search for the Cross was undertaken and the true Cross was identified by a healing miracle.
pass_a_gloss: And immediately he commanded the bishops to make the search for the longed-for wood. And while all were at a loss concerning the place, and one was telling one suspicion, another another, the bishop of the city was urging all to keep quiet and to offer more earnest prayer to God about this. And when this had happened, immediately the place was shown from God to the bishop, in which had been set up the temple and the statue of the unclean demon. Then the queen, using the royal authority, having gathered a great crowd of craftsmen and laborers, commanded the abominable building to be overturned from its foundations, and the earth to be thrown away somewhere far off. And when this had happened, the divine tomb appeared, and the place of the Skull, and not far away three crosses separated; and having searched carefully they found also the nails. From there then perplexity and distress seized the queen, as she was seeking which then might be the Master's Cross. But the bishop through faith resolved the discernment. For to a woman who was ill, one of the notable women, and who had been given up by all, and who was breathing her last, having brought each of the crosses, he found the one being sought; for only the shadow of the saving Cross drew near to the sick woman, immediately the breathless and motionless woman by divine power at once leaped up and with a great voice crying out and glorifying God. And the queen Helena with her voice crying out and glorifying God, with great joy and fear having taken up the life-giving cross, one part with the nails she sent up to her son. And for the rest having made a silver chest, she handed it over to the bishop of the city, for a memorial to all generations, and having ordained that a church be made in the life-giving tomb and on holy Golgotha and in Bethlehem in the cave, where our Lord Jesus Christ underwent the birth according to the flesh, and on the Mount of Olives, where the Lord having blessed the disciples was taken up. And having done many other things in Jerusalem, she returned to her son. And he having received her with joy, having placed the portion of the precious cross in a golden case, handed it over to the bishop for safekeeping, having commanded to celebrate with yearly memorials the exaltation of the precious cross. And of the nails, some he forged into his own helmet, and others he mixed into the bridle of his horse, so that the saying of the Lord spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: 'In that day, what is on the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord Almighty.' And the king wrote to Bishop Macarius to hasten the building, and he sent a ruler of the work with abundance of money, having commanded him that the holy places be built generously, so that there should not be such beauty in all the earth. And he wrote also to the governors of the province to assist the work in every way from the public account, both in money and in expenses and in materials. And the king was joyfully celebrating the feast of the twentieth anniversary, giving thanks to God for all the good things which he had done in the times of his reign. And the years are counted from the coming of Christ until the discovery of the cross, three hundred fifty-two years. And from Adam until the coming of Christ, five thousand five hundred years. But according to others five thousand four hundred seventy-five. And in Aelia Macarius, whose name means blessed was succeeded by Maximonas. And this man was gentle and very distinguished. For in the persecution he endured many tortures for God, and having lost his right eye he was released upon the confession of the faith. And at that time the blessed Helena the queen made an end of life, being eighty years old, having enjoined many things upon her son concerning piety toward Christ. Up to this point let the history be about the discovery of the life-giving cross. And let no one deceive himself, speaking vainly, introducing unprofitable things and myth-makings through strange names into the subject.

choices.why: Keeps the literal noun ξύλου as 'wood' rather than 'Cross' to preserve the source's circumlocution for the Cross before its identification.
Literal rendering; the context makes clear this is Macarius of Jerusalem, but the source uses the periphrasis.

choices.term: τοῦ ἀκαθάρτου δαίμονος ὁ ναὸς καὶ τὸ ἄγαλμα
choices.english: the temple and the image of the unclean demon
choices.why: Literal word order and vocabulary; 'temple' for ναός and 'image' for ἄγαλμα distinguish the pagan shrine from a Christian church.
rejected: the shrine and statue of the unclean demon
the temple and idol of the unclean spirit

choices.why: μυσαρόν means 'abominable, defiled'; 'building' for οἰκοδόμημα keeps the general term rather than specifying a temple.
∆εσποτικός is an adjective from δεσπότης, 'Master/Lord'; 'Master's' preserves the distinct term rather than using 'Lord's' which would blur with Κύριος.
Idiomatic literal rendering of the phrase meaning 'at the point of death'.

bible_refs.note: Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ, ἔσται τὸ ἐπὶ τὸν χαλινὸν τοῦ ἵππου, ἅγιον Κυρίῳ παντοκράτορι

pass_b_english: At once he commanded the bishops to search for the longed-for wood. But all were at a loss about the place, and one told of one suspicion, another of another. The bishop of the city urged them all to keep quiet and to offer more earnest prayer to God about this. When this was done, the place was shown to the bishop from God at once: the place where the temple and the statue of the unclean demon had been set up.

Then the queen, using her imperial authority, gathered a great crowd of craftsmen and laborers and ordered the abominable building to be overturned from its foundations and the earth thrown far away. When this was done, the divine tomb appeared, and Golgotha, the place of the Skull, and not far off three crosses lying apart. Searching carefully, they also found the nails.

From then on, helplessness and distress seized the queen as she sought to know which one was the Master's cross. But the bishop resolved the question through faith. He brought each of the crosses to a woman who was ill, one of the prominent women, given up on by everyone and breathing her last. He found the one he was seeking: for only the shadow of the saving cross drew near the sick woman, and at once she who was breathless and motionless leaped up by divine power on the spot, crying out with a loud voice and glorifying God.

Queen Helena, crying out with a loud voice and glorifying God, took up the life-giving Cross with great joy and fear. One part of it, together with the nails, she sent up to her son. The rest she placed in a silver casket and handed it over to the bishop of the city, as a memorial for all generations. She also decreed that a church be built at the life-giving tomb, and at holy Golgotha, and in Bethlehem in the cave where our Lord Jesus Christ endured birth according to the flesh, and on the Mount of Olives, where the Lord blessed the disciples and was taken up. And after doing many other things in Jerusalem, she returned to her son.

He received her with joy. He placed the portion of the precious Cross that had been sent to him in a golden case and handed it over to the bishop for safekeeping, commanding that the exaltation of the precious Cross be celebrated with annual commemorations. Some of the nails he forged into his own helmet, and the others he mixed into the bridle of his horse, so that what the Lord said through the prophet might be fulfilled: "On that day, what is on the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord Almighty" (Zechariah 14:20).

The emperor wrote to Bishop Macarius to hasten the building, and he sent a superintendent of the work with an abundance of money, instructing him that the holy places be built magnificently, so that there would be no such beauty in all the earth. He also wrote to the governors of the province to assist the work in every way from the public account, with money, expenses, and materials. The emperor was joyfully celebrating the feast of his twentieth anniversary, giving thanks to God for all the good things he had done in the years of his reign.

The years from the coming of Christ to the discovery of the Cross total three hundred fifty-two years. From Adam to the coming of Christ, five thousand five hundred years; according to others, five thousand four hundred seventy-five. In Jerusalem, Macarius, whose name means blessed, was succeeded by Maximonas. He was a gentle man and very distinguished. During the persecution he endured many tortures for God, and after losing his right eye he was released for his confession of the faith.

At that time the blessed Queen Helena reached the end of her life, being eighty years old, after giving many instructions to her son about piety toward Christ. Let the account of the discovery of the life-giving Cross end here. And let no one deceive himself by speaking empty and unprofitable words, or by introducing fictions with strange names into the subject.
notes: The source text contains line-break artifacts: 'σπου δαιοτέραν' for σπουδαιοτέραν, 'οἰκο δόμημα' for οἰκοδόμημα, 'σταυ ροῦ' for σταυροῦ, 'ἀν ελομένη' for ἀνελομένη, 'γλωσ \σόκομον' for γλωσσόκομον, 'μνή ματι' for μνήματι, 'ἀν ελήφθη' for ἀνελήφθη, 'περι κεφαλαίαν' for περικεφαλαίαν, 'συμβα ρίῳ' for συμβαρίῳ, 'ἀποθέμε νος' for ἀποθέμενος. These are treated as line breaks, not textual variants.
The numeral '4081' appears in the source before 'τοῦ τιμίου σταυροῦ μερίδα'; it is likely a marginal note or folio number and is not translated.

problems.why: Glossary maps Aelia to Jerusalem but Κρανίον is not translated; 'Skull' alone obscures this is Golgotha.
problems.fix: Golgotha, the place of the Skull

edits.new: Golgotha, the place of the Skull

problems.why: Reader may not recognize all these refer to same object; 'life-giving' vs 'saving' vs 'precious' vs 'glorious' etc. seem like different categories.
problems.fix: Consistent 'life-giving Cross' or note variants in introduction.

variants.text: the life-giving wood of the glorious Cross
the victorious weapon of the life-giving Cross

problems.why: Same location rendered three ways; reader may think these are different sites.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'holy tomb' or gloss equivalents.

problems.why: Unusual rendering; standard term is 'life-giving tomb' or 'holy sepulcher'; 'God-receiving' suggests tomb received God, which is awkward Christologically.
problems.fix: Use 'life-giving tomb' consistently or 'tomb that received God'.

problems.quote: the image of the unclean demon
problems.why: In context of temple to Aphrodite/Venus at site, 'image' is statue; 'demon' is author's interpretation; reader may think of a specific demon rather than pagan goddess.
problems.fix: Clarify 'the statue of the pagan goddess (whom he calls the unclean demon)'.

problems.quote: "On that day, what is on the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord Almighty" (Zechariah 14:20)
problems.why: Zechariah 14:20 in most Bibles refers to 'bells on the horses' being holy, or 'the pots in the Lord's house'; 'bridle' is a variant or mistranslation of Hebrew 'mitsnephet' or confusion with bells on harness.
problems.fix: Check against LXX; if LXX has 'bridle', note this is Septuagint variant.

problems.quote: Maximonas succeeded Macarius, whose name meant blessed
problems.why: 'Aptly named' and 'name meant blessed' both gloss Macarius's name differently.
problems.fix: Unify: 'Macarius, whose name means blessed' throughout.

edits.old: the place where the temple and the image of the unclean demon had been set up.
edits.new: the place where the temple and the statue of the unclean demon had been set up.

edits.old: In Jerusalem, Maximonas succeeded Macarius, whose name meant blessed.

fixed: The 'life-giving Cross' vs 'saving Cross' vs 'precious Cross' variants are all present in the source (ζωοποιός, σωτήριος, τίμιος) and are intentional rhetorical variation, not a translation inconsistency.
The 'divine tomb' and 'life-giving tomb' are both in the source (θεῖον μνῆμα, ζωοποιῷ μνήματι) and are distinct epithets; no 'God-receiving tomb' appears in the English.
The 'image' has been changed to 'statue' to clarify that it is a physical cult object; the source's 'unclean demon' is retained as the author's polemical interpretation.
The Zechariah quotation follows the Septuagint, which reads 'bridle' (χαλινός) where the Hebrew has 'bells'; this is a legitimate LXX variant, not a mistranslation.
The Macarius name gloss has been unified to 'whose name means blessed' in both the English and the literal gloss.

problems.why: Reader may not recognize 'life-giving wood,' 'saving cross,' 'Master's cross,' 'precious Cross,' 'worshipped Cross' all refer to same object.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'life-giving Cross' or add note.

variants.text: the life-giving wood of the glorious Cross

problems.why: Two different bishops of Jerusalem named; reader may confuse succession or think typo.
problems.fix: Clarify Macarius succeeded Hermonas, then Maximonas succeeded Macarius.

problems.quote: He placed the portion of the precious Cross in a golden case and handed it over to the bishop for safekeeping
problems.why: Contradicts earlier: Helena gave portion to Macarius in silver casket; now Constantine gives to unnamed 'bishop' in golden case.
problems.fix: Clarify textual variant or different portion.

problems.quote: "On that day, what is on the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord Almighty" (Zechariah 14:20)
problems.why: Zechariah 14:20 refers to bells on horses, not nails; Constantine's act is legendary embellishment, not biblical fulfillment.
problems.fix: Note this is typological application, not literal prophecy fulfillment.

problems.quote: On that day, what is on the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord Almighty
problems.why: Zechariah 14:20 reads 'HOLY TO THE LORD' on the bells of the horses, not 'what is on the bridle.'
problems.fix: Check LXX wording; citation may conflate or paraphrase the verse.

problems.why: Multiple epithets for the same Cross may confuse a reader into thinking different crosses or aspects are meant.
problems.fix: Note in introduction that these are rhetorical variations on the same object.

edits.new: He placed the portion of the precious Cross that had been sent to him in a golden case and handed it over to the bishop for safekeeping

fixed: The glossary concern about multiple epithets is stylistic variation in the source; the English already uses the same object consistently, so no change is needed beyond standardizing capitalization in the gloss.

The Zechariah citation is a typological application by the author, not a claim of literal fulfillment; the English already presents it as 'so that what the Lord said through the prophet might be fulfilled,' which matches the source's intent.
The Zechariah wording follows the source's paraphrase; the English already renders the source's wording accurately.

last_rejected.quote: and the earth thrown far away
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ τὸν χοῦν πόῤῥω που ἀποῤῥιφῆναι
last_rejected.why: Source says the earth/dirt was to be thrown far away; English omits 'to be' making it a completed action rather than a command.
last_rejected.fix: and ordered the earth to be thrown far away
last_rejected.ruling: Infinitive ἀποῤῥιφῆναι in indirect command; 'thrown' is standard English equivalent.

last_rejected.quote: "On that day, what is on the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord Almighty" (Zechariah 14:20)
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ, ἔσται τὸ ἐπὶ τὸν χαλινὸν τοῦ ἵππου, ἅγιον Κυρίῳ παντοκράτορι
last_rejected.why: The quote matches Zech 14:20 but the source says 'upon the bridle' (ἐπὶ τὸν χαλινόν), and the English correctly renders it; however, the reference should note this follows the LXX.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'on the bridle' matches ἐπὶ τὸν χαλινόν; LXX note is scholarly addition, not error.

last_rejected.why: Glossary maps 'Aelia' to 'Jerusalem' but English uses 'Golgotha, the place of the Skull' instead of following the source's 'the place of the Skull' as standalone name.
last_rejected.fix: the divine tomb appeared, and the place of the Skull, and Golgotha
last_rejected.ruling: English 'Golgotha, the place of the Skull' accurately renders source 'τοῦ Κρανίου'; no glossary issue here.

last_rejected.why: φερώνυμος means 'bearing the name,' not 'whose name meant.' Macarius means blessed, but the Greek says he 'bore the name' Macarius.
last_rejected.fix: Maximonas succeeded Macarius, bearing that blessed name.
last_rejected.ruling: 'φερώνυμον Μακάριον' = 'named/bearing the name Macarius'; 'whose name meant blessed' is a reasonable explanatory gloss.

last_rejected.why: ὑπέμεινε means 'underwent' or 'endured,' but 'endured birth' is absurd English for the Incarnation; Christ underwent/accepted birth.
last_rejected.fix: underwent His birth according to the flesh
last_rejected.ruling: 'ὑπέμεινε' = 'endured/underwent'; 'endured birth' is within range, not a mistranslation, just awkward.

last_rejected.why: τὸ ἐπὶ τὸν χαλινόν is 'that which is on the bridle,' but the Greek quotation has 'τὸ ἐπὶ τὸν χαλινὸν τοῦ ἵππου' = 'the bells on the bridle' (Hebrew context). English 'what is on' loses the specific object.
last_rejected.fix: the bells on the bridle of the horse shall be holy
last_rejected.ruling: 'τὸ ἐπὶ τὸν χαλινὸν' = 'that on the bridle'; 'what is on' accurately renders it; no specific object lost.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ὁ δὲ μετὰ χαρᾶς αὐτὴν ὑποδεξάμενος
last_rejected.why: The antecedent is unclear: 'He' could be Constantine or Macarius. The Greek ὁ δὲ after Helena's return refers to Constantine (her son, ὁ παῖς), but the English paragraph break and 'He' creates ambiguity.
last_rejected.ruling: 'He' follows 'she returned to her son'; antecedent is clear from context. Paragraph break is stylistic.

last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν μὲν τοῦ τιμίου σταυροῦ μερίδα
last_rejected.why: The Greek specifies 'the one portion' (τὴν μὲν...μερίδα) contrasting with 'the rest' (τῷ δὲ λοιπῷ), but English loses this correlative structure, making the two-part division of the Cross less clear.
last_rejected.fix: The one portion of the precious Cross he placed in a golden case
last_rejected.ruling: 'One part...The rest' preserves τὴν μὲν...τῷ δὲ λοιπῷ correlative; no omission or meaning lost.
